questions.stem:
An estate agent is studying the cost of office space in London. He takes a random sample of 90 offices and calculates the cost, £$x$ per square foot. His results are given in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Cost }(£x) & \text{Frequency }(f) & \text{Midpoint }(£y)\\ \hline 20 \leqslant x < 40 & 12 & 30\\ \hline 40 \leqslant x < 45 & 13 & 42.5\\ \hline 45 \leqslant x < 50 & 25 & 47.5\\ \hline 50 \leqslant x < 60 & 32 & 55\\ \hline 60 \leqslant x < 80 & 8 & 70\\ \hline\end{array}$

(You may use $\sum fy^2 = 226687.5$)

A histogram is drawn for these data and the bar representing $50 \leqslant x < 60$ is 2 cm wide and 8 cm high.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the width and height of the bar representing $20 \leqslant x < 40$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: Width $(w) = 4$ cm
M1: Areas: 16 cm$^2$ represents 32 offices (o.e.) or their $h = \frac{6}{\text{their }w}$ (3sf) or $\frac{8}{3.2}\times 0.6$
A1: So height $(h) = 1.5$ cm
Notes: M1 for a correct calculation of areas $1$ cm$^2 = 2$ offices (o.e.); A1 for $h = 1.5$ cm (Correct answer only 2/2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median cost.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: e.g. $(45)+\frac{20}{25}\times 5$ or $(50)-\frac{5}{25}\times 5$ (o.e.)
A1: $= (£)49$
Notes: M1 for a correct expression without end point. Allow "$n+1$" so e.g. $(45)+\frac{20.5}{25}\times 5$; A1 for 49 or, if $(n+1)$ used, allow 49.1 (Correct answer of 49 only 2/2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Estimate the mean cost of office space for these data.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\frac{\sum fy}{90} = \frac{4420}{90}$
A1: $= (£)49.11$ (or better) (Allow $\frac{442}{9}$ or $49\frac{1}{9}$)
Notes: M1 for an attempt at $\frac{\sum fy}{90}$ with at least 3 correct products of $\sum fy$ or $4000 \leqslant \sum fy \leqslant 5000$; A1 for 49.11 (Allow 49.1 from correct working) (Correct answer only 2/2, 49.1 only M1A0)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Estimate the standard deviation for these data.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: $\sqrt{\frac{226687.5}{90}-\bar{x}^2} = \sqrt{106.8487...}$
A1: $=10.3367 = $ awrt $(£)10.3$
Notes: M1 for a correct expression including $\sqrt{\ }$, ft their mean. Allow use of $s$; A1 for awrt 10.3. Allow $s = $ awrt 10.4 if clearly used. [NB use of 49.1 gives 10.389 $\Rightarrow$ A0] (Correct answer of 10.3 with no working is 2/2)

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) Describe, giving a reason, the skewness.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) B1ft: Mean $\approx$ median so distribution is symmetric (no skew or very little skew) [Allow mean > median or $k(\bar{x}-Q_2)$ ($k>0$) so +ve skew if compatible with their figures] [If using quartiles we must see $Q_1=44.0$ and $Q_3=55.5$ used]
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1ft for reason and "symmetric" (or other correct) statement [Allow positive skew] Allow ft of their (b) and their (c). For "symmetric" need $|\bar{x}-Q_2|<1$ "correlation" is B0

parts.label: f
parts.text:
Rika suggests that the cost of office space in London can be modelled by a normal distribution with mean £50 and standard deviation £10
(f) With reference to your answer to part (e), comment on Rika's suggestion.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(f) B1ft: Symmetric (or little skew) so normal (or Rika's suggestion) may be suitable
Notes: B1ft Suggest normal is or isn't suitable with suitable reason based on (e) or mean and median

parts.label: g
parts.text:
(g) Use Rika's model to estimate the 80th percentile of the cost of office space in London.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(g) M1: $\frac{c-50}{10}=0.8416$ [N.B. use of $(1-0.8416)$ is B0]
B1: for using $z = \pm 0.8416$ or better (calc gives 0.8416212...) in standardised attempt e.g. $\sqrt{10}$ for 10
A1: $c=58.416 = (£)58.42$ awrt $58.4$
Notes: M1 for stand'ing using "$c$", 50 and 10 and setting equal to $\pm$ z value where $0.84 \leqslant z \leqslant 0.85$; B1 for using $z=\pm0.8416$ or better; A1 for awrt 58.4 (accept 3sf here) (Ans only 58.4 is M1B0A1 but 58.416 or better is 3/3)

questions.stem:
The Venn diagram shows three events $A$, $B$ and $C$, where $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ and $t$ are probabilities.

[Venn diagram showing circles $A$, $B$, $C$ with region $t$ in $B$ only, $s$ in $A\cap B$ only, $p$ in $B\cap C$ only, $r$ in $A$ only, $q$ in $C$ only, and $0.08$ outside all circles]

$\mathrm{P}(A) = 0.5$, $\mathrm{P}(B) = 0.6$ and $\mathrm{P}(C) = 0.25$ and the events $B$ and $C$ are independent.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: $p = \mathrm{P}(B\cap C) = \mathrm{P}(B)\times\mathrm{P}(C) = 0.6\times 0.25 = 0.15$
A1: $q = [\mathrm{P}(C)-p] = 0.10$
Notes: M1 for a correct expression (using independence) for $p$ or 0.15; A1 for $q=0.10$ (both correct 2/2)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $r = 1-0.08-[\mathrm{P}(B)+q] = 1-0.08-0.6-0.1$ (o.e.) or $1-0.08-(0.6+0.25-p)$
A1cao: $=0.22$
Notes: Mark (b) & (c) together. M1 for a correct expression for $r$ using $\mathrm{P}(B\cup C)$. Can ft their $q\in[0,0.32]$; A1cao for $r=0.22$ (correct ans only 2/2)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- ALT Find t then s then r: (b) M1 for $r = \mathrm{P}(A) - s$ and the A1 for 0.22

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence write down the value of $s$ and the value of $t$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) B1ft: $s = [\mathrm{P}(A)-r] = 0.28$
B1ft: $t = [\mathrm{P}(B)-p-s]$ or use $\mathrm{P}(B\cap C')-s = 0.6\times0.75-"0.28" = 0.17$
Notes: 1st B1ft for $s=0.28$ or $0.5-$ their "0.22"; 2nd B1ft for $t=0.17$ or $0.6-$their"0.15"$-$their"0.28". ALT: Find $t$ then $s$ then $r$: 2nd B1 for $t=0.17$ [from $1-0.08-\mathrm{P}(A)-\mathrm{P}(C)$]; 1st B1ft for $s=0.28$ or $\mathrm{P}(B)-$"0.17"$-$"0.15"
Official notes (completeness pass):
- s = 0.3: They assume A and B are independent and get s = 0.3 [from $\mathrm{P}(A)\times\mathrm{P}(B)$] (c) 1st B0 for s = 0.3 BUT can get 2nd B1ft for either case in the scheme (b) M1 for $r = \mathrm{P}(A) - s$ BUT then A0cao for r = 0.2
- Fully correct Venn diagram will score the first 6 marks. If text and VD disagree use text values

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) State, giving a reason, whether or not the events $A$ and $B$ are independent.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: $\mathrm{P}(A)\times\mathrm{P}(B) = 0.5\times 0.6 = 0.3$ which is not equal to $s$ ($=0.28$)
A1: So $A$ and $B$ are not independent
Notes: M1 for a correct calculation of $\mathrm{P}(A)\times\mathrm{P}(B)=0.5\times0.6$ or 0.3 and a clear comparison with their $s(\neq 0.3)$ Or calculation of $\mathrm{P}(A|B)=\frac{7}{15}$ or 0.467 or $\frac{\text{their }s}{0.6}$ and comparison with $\mathrm{P}(A)=0.5$ (o.e.); A1 dep. on M1 being earned and clear statement that $A$ and $B$ are not independent
Official notes (completeness pass):
- SC s = 0.3 dep on 1st B1ft for s = 0.5 – 0.2 in (c); for correct calc. and conclusion seen (B1). On epen M0A1

parts.label: e
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) M1: $\frac{(s+p)\text{ or }(0.6-t)}{\mathrm{P}(A\cup C)\text{ or }[\mathrm{P}(A)+\mathrm{P}(C)]\text{ or }(r+s+p+q)} = \frac{"0.28"+"0.15"\text{ or }0.6-"0.17"}{0.5+0.25}$
A1ft: for correct ratio or ft using their values in numerator but correct denominator
A1: $=\frac{43}{75}$
Notes: M1 for a correct ratio expression of probs: num. < den. Allow $1-(0.08+\text{their }"t")$ on den. Any sight of multiplication on the numerator e.g. $0.6\times0.75$ is M0; 1st A1ft for correct ratio or ft using their values in numerator but correct denominator; 2nd A1 for $\frac{43}{75}$ or accept awrt 0.573

questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $X$ has probability distribution

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2\\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X=x) & a & b & b & c\\ \hline\end{array}$

The cumulative distribution function of $X$ is given by

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2\\ \hline \mathrm{F}(x) & \frac{1}{3} & d & \frac{5}{6} & e\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: $a=\frac{1}{3}$ and $e=1$
B1: $c=\left[1-\frac{5}{6}\right]=\frac{1}{6}$
M1: "$\frac{1}{3}$"$+2b=\frac{5}{6}$ or "$\frac{1}{3}$"$+2b+$"$\frac{1}{6}$"$=1$
A1: $\Rightarrow b=\frac{1}{4}$
B1ft: $d=a+b=$"$\frac{1}{3}$"$+$"$\frac{1}{4}$" or $d=\frac{5}{6}-$"$\frac{1}{4}$" (o.e.) so $d=\frac{7}{12}$
Notes: Probabilities not in $[0,1]$ score 0 for corresponding A or B marks. Allow exact decimals or equivalent fractions. If answers in the table and answers on the page disagree take the answers on the page. If jumbled working is followed by a list of answers on the page mark the list. M1 for an equation for $b$. Follow through their value of $a$ and possibly $c$ if both in $[0,1]$. Must be seen as an equation with $b$ the only unknown. NB $b=d-a$ is not a suitable equation and use of this is M0. 1st A1 for $b=\frac{1}{4}$ or 0.25 (Correct answer only is 2/2). 3rd B1ft for $d=\frac{7}{12}$ or their $a+$their $b$ but their $d$ must satisfy $\frac{1}{3}<d<\frac{5}{6}$

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1ft: $[\mathrm{P}(X^2=1)=a+b=]\frac{7}{12}$
Notes: B1ft for $\frac{7}{12}$ or their $a+$their $b$ or their $d$. Please check the two B1ft marks carefully

questions.stem: Yuto works in the quality control department of a large company. The time, $T$ minutes, it takes Yuto to analyse a sample is normally distributed with mean 18 minutes and standard deviation 5 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that Yuto takes longer than 20 minutes to analyse the next sample.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: $[\mathrm{P}(T>20)=]\ \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{20-18}{5}\right)$
M1: $\mathrm{P}(Z>0.4)=1-0.6554$
A1: $=0.3446$ or awrt $0.345$
Notes: 1st M1 for standardising with 20, 18 and 5. Accept $\pm$; 2nd M1 for attempting $1-p$ where $0.5<p<0.7$. Beware $1-0.4$ (or their $z$ value) is M0; A1 for awrt 0.345 (Correct ans only 3/3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The company has a large store of samples analysed by Yuto with the time taken for each analysis recorded. Serena is investigating the samples that took Yuto longer than 15 minutes to analyse.
She selects, at random, one of the samples that took Yuto longer than 15 minutes to analyse.
(b) Find the probability that this sample took Yuto more than 20 minutes to analyse.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Require $\mathrm{P}(T>20\mid T>15)$ or $\frac{\mathrm{P}(T>20)}{\mathrm{P}(T>15)}$
M1: $\frac{"(a)"}{\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{15-18}{5}\right)} = \frac{"(a)"}{\mathrm{P}(Z>-0.6)}$
A1ft: $=\frac{"0.3446"}{0.7257}$ or $\frac{"0.345"}{0.726}$
A1: $=0.47485...=$ awrt $0.475$
Notes: 1st M1 for either correct conditional probability statement (allow "in words" or any letter except $Z$) 1st M1 can be implied by 2nd M1 so a mark of M0M1 should not be given; 2nd M1 for using their (a) on num. and attempting to standardise $\mathrm{P}(T>15)$ (no $\pm$) on denom. Num.>Deno. is M0. Allow one digit transcription errors from (a) e.g. 0.3464 or 0.3466 etc for 2nd M1 and 1st A1ft; 1st A1ft for their 0.3446 on numerator and denominator of 0.7257 (or better: 0.7257469...) provided Num < Denom. Allow 0.726 on the denominator. Sight of $\frac{"0.3446"}{0.7257\text{ or }0.726}$ will score M1M1A1ft; 2nd A1 for awrt 0.475

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Serena can identify, in advance, the samples that Yuto can analyse in under 15 minutes and in future she will assign these to someone else.
(c) Estimate the median time taken by Yuto to analyse samples in future.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\mathrm{P}(T>d\mid T>15)=0.5$ or $\mathrm{P}(T<d\mid T>15)=0.5$
A1ft: $\mathrm{P}(T>d)$ or $\mathrm{P}(15<T<d)=0.5\times"0.7257"=[0.36285]$
M1: $\mathrm{P}(T<d)="0.63715"$
A1: So $\frac{d-18}{5}=0.35$ (calculator gives 0.35085...)

questions.question_text:
Yuto works in the quality control department of a large company. The time, $T$ minutes, it takes Yuto to analyse a sample is normally distributed with mean 18 minutes and standard deviation 5 minutes.
(a) Find the probability that Yuto takes longer than 20 minutes to analyse the next sample.
(3)
The company has a large store of samples analysed by Yuto with the time taken for each analysis recorded. Serena is investigating the samples that took Yuto longer than 15 minutes to analyse.
She selects, at random, one of the samples that took Yuto longer than 15 minutes to analyse.
(b) Find the probability that this sample took Yuto more than 20 minutes to analyse.
(4)
Serena can identify, in advance, the samples that Yuto can analyse in under 15 minutes and in future she will assign these to someone else.
(c) Estimate the median time taken by Yuto to analyse samples in future.
